params.env_note: local, reduced size (registry env aws-scale); workstation shared with SC-07 (Flux query timings)

notes: profile default; 15 cases; local reduced-size run (registry env aws-scale), workstation shared with SC-07 (Flux query timings) running at the same time

limits.finding: [default loss5_nospool] without spool, 11700 rows lost while the queues had room: writes that timed out or were cut (11700 uncertain rows, 0 of them stored by InfluxDB anyway); counted, never retried
limits.proposal: Set spool_dir on links that time out (uncertain writes are then replayed, idempotent); or retry uncertain writes in memory once, since InfluxDB writes are idempotent

limits.finding: [default loss20_nospool] without spool, 37100 rows lost while the queues had room: writes that timed out or were cut (38350 uncertain rows, 1250 of them stored by InfluxDB anyway); counted, never retried
limits.proposal: Set spool_dir on links that time out (uncertain writes are then replayed, idempotent); or retry uncertain writes in memory once, since InfluxDB writes are idempotent

limits.finding: [default bw1mbit_t30_nospool] without spool, 12300 rows dropped beyond max_queue_rows (counted): the link wrote less than the 2000 rows/s offered
limits.proposal: Expected behaviour of the bound; size max_queue_rows for the longest degraded period, or set spool_dir

limits.finding: [default bw1mbit_t30_spool] with spool, 10550 rows dropped beyond max_queue_rows (counted): the link kept answering, slower than the traffic, so the storage was never unavailable and the spool did not take the overflow
limits.proposal: With spool_dir, spool the oldest batches beyond max_queue_rows instead of dropping them (bounded by spool_max_bytes)
